courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So now in this module, we had a look at native device features and you learned that Capacitor is
not only the tool that wraps your web app but also the tool that provides a bridge to native APIs
that allow you to access the camera or the location.
You also learned that with the help of the pwa tools, you can get a similar functionality in the browser,
at least if your device supports it and has a camera
and also how you can provide a fallback.
Now these are all tools, you can of course now mix and match in your applications as you need them.
Not every application is built-in the same way,
you might need more robust error handling or handle different scenarios in your app
but I hope that this module helps you understand Capacitor and how you may use it
and I can only encourage you to play around with the many core APIs it exposes to you as well as the
community plugins you can install, also check the plugin installation documentation for that.
And with that, you have a lot of power at your hands
that should allow you to build any mobile app you want.
